newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks edge higher at the open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks edge higher at the open.

* Toronto stocks edged higher at the open on Tuesday as
falling golds were more than offset by rising industrials and
transportation. * 5.8 million shares traded worth C$82.3 million.
Toronto stocks edged higher at the open on Tuesday as falling golds were more than offset by stronger industrials and transportation stocks.
Traders said cautious investors were sticking to large capitalization stocks and a lot of subgroups were hovering around unchanged in thin early trade.
"My sneaking suspicion is the market ends up down today," one trader said.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 5.34 points at the open to 6644.94 in turnover of 5.8 million shares worth C$82.3 million.
Eight of Toronto's 14 sub-indexes gained ground, led by transportation and industrials.
Transportation gained 87.58 points or 1.09 percent to 8158.35 as Laidlaw Inc rose 0.50 to 21 in healthy trade.
Gold led the losers, shedding 60.01 points or 0.78 percent to 7651.07.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Placer Dome Inc rose 0.40 to 20.70 in healthy trade after the gold producer said it would report "substantially reduced" costs of gold production in the first half compared to 1996 when results are released on July 22. The gold producer said its share of average cash production costs for the first six months of 1997 was expected to be US$214 per ounce compared with US$246 an ounce in 1996.

* Shares in IPSCO Inc rose 2.30 to 52.70 in thin trade after the steelmaker reported second-quarter earnings of C$1.11 a share compared to C$0.62 in the year earlier period. IPSCO said results were boosted by firming prices and a shorter than usual spring breakup period, which translated into unexpectedly high oil country tubular shipments in Canada.
